blocks.text: Matthew 19 gathers teaching and encounters on marriage, divorce, eunuchs, children, possessions, and the cost of following Jesus. Jesus answers a test about divorce by appealing to creation and then addresses Moses' provision in relation to human hardness of heart. He welcomes children, challenges a wealthy man to give to the poor and follow him, teaches about the difficulty riches pose for entering the kingdom, and promises the disciples a future role while warning that first and last will be reversed.

sections.title: Disputed sayings within the teaching sequence

blocks.text: Matthew 19 preserves disputed language about the divorce exception and a threefold saying about eunuchs. The chapter places these sayings within teaching on marriage, children, and discipleship, but the supplied context does not settle every interpretive question. The repeated discourse-ending formulas elsewhere in Matthew also organize teaching collections without proving one universally accepted symbolic outline.
